text:
You seized the Goddess's thick hair

With such vigor that everyone would have taken you,

Seeing that haughty air and that beautiful abandon,

For a young ruffian striking his lover.


Your gaze set aflame by a precocious fire,

You displayed your craftsman's pride without shame

In those constructions whose correct audacity

Anticipates the fruits of your maturity.


Poet, our blood escapes through every pore.

Perhaps by chance the Centaur's garment,

Which transformed each vein into a funereal stream,


Was dyed three times in the subtle lavas

Of those monstrous, vengeful reptiles

That Hercules one day strangled in his cradle?

translation.title: To Théodore de Banville
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Baudelaire's violent compliment to Banville's craft and mythic imagery.
